questions.q_en:

The research team is conducting experiments on a new drug that could revolutionise the treatment of the disease.
options_en: Experiments have been conducted on a new drug that could have revolutionised the treatment of the disease through the research team.
Experiments were being conducted on a new drug that could revolutionise the treatment of the disease by the research team.
Experiments are conducted on a new drug that could revolutionise the treatment of the disease from the research team.
Experiments are being conducted on a new drug that could revolutionise the treatment of the disease by the research team.
questions.solution_en:
· The active voice sentence is in present continuous tense ("is conducting").

· To convert it to passive voice, we follow the structure:

Object + is/are being + past participle + by + subject

· Option 4 correctly follows this structure:

"Experiments are being conducted on a new drug that could revolutionise the treatment of the disease by the research team."

· Option 1 changes the tense incorrectly.

· Option 2 uses past continuous, which is incorrect.

· Option 3 has an incorrect structure and wording.

Thus, option 4 is the correct answer.

Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Fort Hare was more than that: it was a beacon for African scholars from all over Southern Central and Eastern Africa.

B. Until 1960, the University College of Fort Hare, in the municipality of Alice, about twenty miles due east from Heald town, was the only residential center of higher education for blacks in South Africa.

C. For young black South Africans like myself, it was Oxford and Cambridge, Harvard and Yale, all rolled into one.

D. The regent was anxious for me to attend Fort Hare and I was gratified to be accepted there. I felt that I was being groomed for success in the world.
questions.solution_en:
Sentence B will come first as it introduces the topic of discussion - 'University College of Fort Hare' and mentions that it was the only residential center of higher education for blacks in South Africa.

Sentence A comes next and tells that it was not only the center of higher education for blacks, but also a beacon for scholars from all over Southern, Central and Eastern Africa. Sentence C follows and mentions what the college meant for the author.

Sentence D concludes and mentions that the author was thankful to be accepted there.

So, the correct order is BACD.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate order of the segments in the options that will fill in the blanks and make a coherent sentence.

Though Rahul prefers eating at home, __________ / __________ / __________ / __________.
options_en: he decided to try a new restaurant yesterday / so much so that / and to his delight, the food was exceptional / he plans to visit it again this weekend
and to his delight, the food was exceptional / so much so that / he decided to try a new restaurant yesterday / he plans to visit it again this weekend
he decided to try a new restaurant yesterday / and to his delight, the food was exceptional / so much so that / he plans to visit it again this weekend
so much so that / he plans to visit it again this weekend / he decided to try a new restaurant yesterday / and to his delight, the food was exceptional
questions.solution_en:
The correct coherent sentence is:

"Though Rahul prefers eating at home, he decided to try a new restaurant yesterday, and to his delight, the food was exceptional, so much so that he plans to visit it again this weekend."

First Segment: "He decided to try a new restaurant yesterday" introduces the action Rahul took.

Second Segment: "And to his delight, the food was exceptional" describes his reaction to the experience.

Third Segment: "So much so that" connects the previous statement to the consequence.

Fourth Segment: "He plans to visit it again this weekend" provides the conclusion of the narrative.

Option a): Incorrect because "so much so that" appears before "and to his delight, the food was exceptional," disrupting the logical flow.

Option b): Incorrect because "and to his delight, the food was exceptional" precedes "he decided to try a new restaurant yesterday," which disrupts the sequence of events.

Option d): Incorrect because "so much so that" comes at the beginning, which lacks proper context and makes the sentence illogical.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

Finally, sentence C provides a conclusion by stating the ultimate benefit of "Finding one's Ikigai," linking it to a fulfilling and longer life, which neatly summarizes the importance of the concept discussed in sentences B, A, and D.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.q_en:
Directions [Set of 4 Questions]: Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

The introduction of African cheetahs to India was planned without considering their spatial ecology, according to researchers who warn that the released animals may come into conflict with people in the neighbouring villages. Spatial ecology addresses the fundamental effects of space on the movement of individual species and on the stability of multispecies communities. A total of 20 cheetahs from Namibia and South Africa were introduced to Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh last year to establish a free-ranging population - for the first time since their extinction in India 70 years ago. Scientists of the Cheetah Research Project of Leibniz-IZW in Namibia argue that in southern Africa, cheetahs live in a stable socio-spatial system with widely spread territories and densities of less than one individual per 100 square kilometres (km²). The plan for cheetahs in Kuno National Park assumes that the high prey density will sustain high cheetah densities, even though there is no evidence for that, they said. In a letter published in the journal Conservation Science and Practice on Thursday, researchers noted that as Kuno National Park is small, it is likely that the released animals will move far beyond the park's boundaries and cause conflicts with neighbouring villages.

According to a calculation of the local prey density, it was calculated that 21 adult cheetahs could be sustained by the prey base in Kuno National Park - equivalent to a density of about three individuals per 100 km². Based on their research results from a long-term study of the spatial behaviour of cheetahs in Namibia, as well as comparable work in East Africa, scientists from the Leibniz Institute for Zoo and Leibniz-IZW warn against overestimating the carrying capacity of the area. The carrying capacity is usually between 0.2 and 1 adult per 100 km² for cheetahs under natural conditions. This is true not only for Namibia but also for the ecologically very different conditions in the Serengeti ecosystem in East Africa which has a much higher density of prey, they said. The team formulated predictions about the spatial behaviour of cheetahs in their new habitat, identifying controversial issues and hidden core assumptions of the reintroduction plan. These assumptions ignore important aspects of the cheetah socio-spatial system.

Read the statements given below.

A. The carrying capacity of 3 cheetahs per 100 km square is currently feasible in Kuno National Park.

B. The carrying capacity for cheetahs is different in Kuno national park when compared to carrying capacity of parks in Africa.
options_en: Both A and B are true but B is not the correct reason for A.
Both A and B are true and B is the correct reason for A.
A is false and B is true.
A is true and B is false.
questions.solution_en:
Statement A is false. The first sentence of the second paragraph states that "According to a calculation of the local prey density, it was calculated that 21 adult cheetahs could be sustained by the prey base in Kuno National Park - equivalent to a density of about three individuals per 100 km²." According to this, the carrying capacity for Kuno National Park is 3 cheetahs per 100 km². The second paragraph also states that "The carrying capacity is usually between 0.2 and 1 adult per 100 km² for cheetahs under natural conditions." So, as per the passage, the current carrying capacity may not be feasible.

Statement B is true. The last sentence of the first paragraph suggests that Kuno National Park is small, and cheetahs might move far beyond the park's boundaries and cause conflicts with neighbouring villages. So, the carrying capacity of Kuno National Park is not the same as in Africa. The third and fourth sentences in the second paragraph corroborate this.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Directions : Read the given passage and answer the question that follows.

As a result of increasing population and expansion of residential areas, forest lands are being encroached. This is not all; even the wildlife is under extreme threat. As our fauna is facing a dearth of adequate shelter in forests, they are heading towards towns and hence get killed by hunters. Consequently, many animal species have either become extinct or are on the verge of extinction. The Black Buck is almost endangered and found only in two countries, Nepal and India. In India, this antelope is found in many national parks like Guindy National Park, Point Calimere and Vellandu sanctuaries of Tamil Nadu, Rollapadu of Andra Pradesh, few parts of Rajasthan and Haryana. As far as their habitat is concerned, they live in open grasslands, dry areas or thinly populated areas and near water resources. They live in the desert areas of Rajasthan and coastal areas because they cannot sustain cold climate. They are the fastest running animals on this planet. Further, this animal is active during the day but slows down in its activities after midday. They are social beings. Hence, they move with their herds, which can vary from 3 to 23 mates. They cohabit twice in a year and give birth twice in a year. Prior to independence, this antelope was extensively hunted which affected their population so much that this species has reached the stage of extinction in many parts of the country. Poachers kill them mainly for material gain. Its skin has an enormous value in the market. In order to protect this species, the IUCN has declared this species nearly threatened. Hence, under Schedule I of the Wildlife Protection Act of 1972, numerous stern measures have been taken. To specify a few, Kaimur Wildlife Sanctuary (Bihar), Gir Forest National Park, Velavadar Wildlife Sanctuary (Gujarat), National Chambal Sanctuary, etc. Despite these acts, hunting is adversely affecting our wildlife. There are some solutions to this problem but the best one is to boycott the products made from endangered species at an international level. This seems to be effective but will it prevent animal hunting? That's a question.

What is the author's tone in this passage?
questions.solution_en:
The author's tone is concerned, as the passage highlights the serious issues of forest encroachment, wildlife threats, and the near-endangered status of the Black Buck. The author expresses worry about the extinction of species, stating, "Consequently, many animal species have either become extinct or are on the verge of extinction," and notes the adverse effects of hunting despite conservation efforts: "Despite these acts, hunting is adversely affecting our wildlife." The suggestion to boycott products and the rhetorical question, "This seems to be effective but will it prevent animal hunting? That's a question," further indicate a tone of concern about the future of wildlife.

(a) Revengeful: A revengeful tone would imply a desire for retaliation or vengeance, which is absent. The author does not express anger or a call for punishment but focuses on concern and solutions (e.g., boycotting products).

(b) Impressed: An impressed tone would suggest admiration or approval, which is inappropriate given the passage's focus on negative issues like extinction and poaching, not positive achievements.

(c) Agitated: An agitated tone implies intense anger or restlessness, but the passage maintains a measured, informative style, expressing worry rather than outrage, as seen in the calm proposal of solutions.

Hence, the correct answer is option (4).

questions.solution_en:

a) Detraction - Correct, as it means the act of diminishing the worth, reputation, or importance of someone or something.

b) Support - Opposite of the idiom's meaning; it means to help or encourage.

c) Criticism - While the act might be criticized, the idiom itself isn't about criticizing.

d) Applause - Opposite, as the act aims to take applause away from another.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

It's funny how every time he fails to apply the ____ and the _____ glass.
questions.solution_en:
The sentence requires two words to fill the blanks, and the context suggests a play on homophones "brakes" and "breaks."

"Brakes" refers to a device for slowing or stopping (e.g., in a vehicle).

"Breaks" means to shatter or fracture (e.g., a glass breaking).

The sentence likely describes a scenario where someone fails to apply the "brakes" (e.g., in a car), causing something (like a glass) to "break."

Checking the options:

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

She can swim very well, __________?
questions.solution_en:
This is a tag question structure, where the helping verb "can" in the positive statement is transformed into "can't" [negative] for the tag question to maintain the appropriate polarity. The tag question "can't she?" is used to seek confirmation or agreement with the preceding statement about her ability to swim very well.

Other options do not conform to the criteria that 'can' should be used and the subject and the verb should invert their positions.

The complete sentence is - "She can swim very well, can't she."

Hence, option (a) is correct.

questions.q_en:
Identify the segment in the given sentence which contains the grammatical error.

If India will win this match they will win the series.
questions.solution_en:
The given sentence is an example of the first conditional sentence. The sentence structure of a first conditional sentence is: if + simple present, will/can/must + verb.

The given sentence is incorrect according to the syntax of the sentence. The verb 'will win' should be replaced with the singular form of the verb (because the subject 'India' is singular in nature) 'wins' to rectify the given sentence. Therefore, the error is in the part in option (a).

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: If India wins this match, they will win the series.

questions.solution_en: While changing the voice of a sentence, the place of the subject and the object is changed and no change is made in the tense of the subject. The sentence is in the passive form and contains two clauses. The voice of both clauses needs to be changed in such cases. 1st clause- 'Is/am/are + being + past participle' will change into 'is/am/are + present participle'. 2nd clause- 'Modal verb + verb + be + past participle' will change into 'modal + base form of verb'. Option C is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Directions [Set of 4 Questions]: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

In the part of Italy that is known as Umbria, there stands the little town of Assisi, built on the slopes of Monte Subasio. Assisi is a very old city - some say it dates as far back as 400 or 500 B.C. - and underneath its streets are long passages that come out far away in the hills, as if the citizens had used them in times of siege as a means of escape. If you studied its ruins of temples, theatres, and circuses, you would learn a great deal of history, not only of Assisi itself but of Rome as well. Totila, the Goth, halted there for a short time on his way to besiege the Eternal City. Charlemagne passed through it two hundred and fifty years later; while in the struggle for power between the pope and the emperor during the Middle Ages, the town sided first with one and then with the other. But, against one enemy, the people of Assisi never ceased fighting, and that was with the citizens of Perugia, which lay across the hills and could be seen plainly from the castle on the top. Among all the merchants of Assisi, none was so rich or well thought of as Bernadone, who carried on with France a large trade in silk and embroidered stuff. He had an only son, Giovanni, or John, born in 1182, and, as soon as the child was four or five years old, he had been taught French, so that by and by his father might send him across the sea to sell his goods to the noble ladies of the French court, and as no one in Assisi ever thought of learning any language but Italian, the boy was nicknamed "Il Francesco," or "the Frenchman." This nickname would become symbolic of a remarkable future. Giovanni would grow up to transform not only his own life but also the lives of countless others, embodying values of humility and compassion that continue to resonate around the world.

How did the town of Assisi align during the power struggle between the pope and the emperor in the Middle Ages?
options_en: It maintained an impartial stance throughout the conflict.
It alternated its support between the two opposing sides.
It consistently backed the papal authority.
It uniformly supported the imperial forces.
questions.solution_en: The passage mentions, 'while in the struggle for power between the pope and the emperor during the Middle Ages, the town sided first with one and then with the other.' This indicates that Assisi shifted its support between the pope and the emperor, rather than maintaining a consistent stance or uniformly supporting one side (options c and d). The passage explicitly suggests that Assisi did not maintain an impartial stance (option a). Hence, (b) is the correct answer.
